- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model should not overreact — cap forecast slope to avoid overshoot; reduce rate of increase by 10–20%.
- If official event net is bearish (supply net <0) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model should not ignore downward pressure — shift forecast mean 2–5% lower than baseline.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed or negative — model should not hold upward trend longer than 3–5 days after peak.
- When sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., -0.50, -1.00), model should reduce forecast volatility and add downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model should not ignore supply net — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per event if supply net is negative.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early reversal (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), apply “early correction” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.
